# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about this carefully. I have the manual, but I can only communicate via gestures to Deaf (who sees the bomb). I cannot speak, so Blind (who must actually cut the wire) can never hear me directly. I need to relay information through Deaf, but Deaf cannot speak either—wait, let me check the turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf. Deaf speaks and can be heard by whoever comes after in the round, but Deaf is last, so Deaf's speech this round reaches only next round's Mute (me). That's a full cycle.

Actually the real bridge is: I gesture to Deaf (since Deaf can see). Deaf can speak (to Blind, who can hear). So the chain is Mute --gesture--> Deaf --speak--> Blind. That works, but takes turns.

Right now I have no info about which light is actually on, so I can't send anything useful yet. I should wait, but first establish that I'm ready and encode the manual mapping using gestures for later use, once Deaf reports the light color. But Deaf hasn't spoken yet - I go first this round, before Blind and Deaf. I have no info from them yet.

I'll wait this turn since I have nothing to relay yet.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows 0. Light is yellow. There is one large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: 1 is red, 2 is blue, 3 is green.

Now I know the light is yellow, so per the manual the correct cut wire color is blue. Deaf said light is yellow and wire 2 is blue. I need to get this to Blind, but I can't speak — only Deaf can speak to Blind. I can only gesture to Deaf. I need to establish a gesture code that tells Deaf which wire color is correct, so Deaf can then relay via speech to Blind.

Since Deaf already knows the wire colors and positions (they can see), I just need to signal to Deaf which color/number is the correct cut, using gestures. I'll establish a simple convention: point to wire number using finger-count-like gestures. Let's use ☝ (one), ✌ (two), 🤟(three) as numbers 1,2,3 to indicate wire number. Wire 2 is blue, which matches yellow→blue. So I signal "2" to Deaf.

I should also clarify this is my first gesture code, so I'll try to make intent clear: pointing at wire 2. Let me send ✌ alone as "wire two is correct" - but Deaf needs to interpret this correctly without prior established code. I'll take the risk and hope simple numeric gesture works, since I have no other channel.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display shows 0, light is yellow, wires are 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green, one button labeled push to defuse.

Blind has relayed to me what Deaf said via speech (Blind can hear Deaf). This confirms the chain: Deaf speaks, Blind hears it, and Blind can also speak to me? Wait, turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf — so Blind speaks before Deaf in the round, but this message says "Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports..." — meaning Blind is relaying something Deaf told them in a previous round via speech. So Deaf CAN speak to Blind, and Blind can speak to me. Good, this confirms a full communication loop exists.

Now Blind is asking me (implicitly, by repeating the bomb state) what to do — Blind needs to know which wire to cut. Blind cannot see gestures, so my gesture to Deaf won't directly reach Blind — but Deaf can then speak to Blind. However, this round order is Mute, Blind, Deaf — I already sent my gesture last turn, and this turn I go first again.

I know: light yellow → cut blue wire → wire 2. I need Deaf to tell Blind "cut wire 2" or "cut the blue wire". Since I can't speak, I must gesture to Deaf now, reinforcing wire 2, and trust Deaf to then speak the instruction to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I did not receive any gesture, I only hear speech. Please tell me directly in words: which wire to cut, or whether to push the button. I need a clear instruction I can act on.
Deaf says to Mute: I see wire 2 is blue. Is wire 2 the one to cut? Gesture thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌]

Deaf is asking me to confirm wire 2 with thumbs up/down. I can gesture that. Blind is asking me directly for a spoken instruction, but I cannot speak — Blind needs to get the instruction from Deaf instead. I need to make this clear, but I can't speak to Blind. I can only gesture to Deaf. I should confirm wire 2 to Deaf with 👍, and trust Deaf to then relay "cut wire 2" to Blind via speech.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Nothing new arrived this turn. I've already confirmed wire 2 (blue) to Deaf with a thumbs up. Deaf should now relay this to Blind via speech since Deaf comes after Blind but before me in the turn order — wait, actually order is Mute, Blind, Deaf, so Deaf speaks last in the round, reaching Blind only next round. I should just wait now since I have nothing new to send; my confirmation is already in transit to Deaf, who will need to speak to Blind next.

```
wait()
```
